subject: The completed opt-in briefing skill for HTML and Markdown with linked evidence and anchored reader feedback
reader: Parker approved the plan and wants to see the result and understand what was tested

sections.heading: Briefing
sections.text:
When you ask an agent for a summary, an engineering explanation or a decision, it can now use the same briefing pattern in HTML or Markdown. The new skill keeps the explanation in front of you, gives evidence its own linked notes, and keeps your comments attached to the passage you were reading. 

 Ready to use 
Invoke briefing by name. The current briefing skills remain available under their existing names.

legend.0: Nothing. Every term the passage leans on is either ordinary English or is explained in the passage at the point it is first used. The reader follows it from the first sentence to the last without stopping.
legend.1: One or two things are named without being explained — a file, a component, a product — but the sentences around them make their role clear enough that the reader keeps going without losing the thread.
legend.2: Several names or terms arrive unexplained, so the reader follows the argument only by taking them on trust.
legend.3: The passage is written for somebody already inside the project. Its central sentences cannot be understood at all without knowledge the document has not supplied anywhere.

sections.heading: 01 Choose the Brief
sections.text:
The agent chooses the purpose separately from the medium, using the reader and reading budget you give it. It can infer those choices from the task; a different kind of brief is valid when its job is clear. 
 01 · Two independent choices 

 What should it do? 
Summary 
Engineering 
Decision 
Explain what happened, show how it works, or help you choose. 
 How should you read it? 
HTML 
Markdown 
MP4 · reserved 
HTML is the visual default. Markdown keeps the short reading and linked support. 
 A decision can be Markdown; an engineering brief can be HTML. Purpose guides the content without prescribing a section template. 

Try the same engineering explanation as HTML or Markdown .

sections.heading: 02 Follow the Evidence
sections.text:
A short explanation still needs support. The skill defaults to a deep chain of evidence, with tests and source for code claims. You can ask for a shallower chain while the brief itself stays concise. 
 02 · Support behind links Evidence depth Sources Reasoning Code trace · default 
 Source 
 What was built and checked . 
 Reasoning 
 What these checks establish, and what remains untested . 
 Code trace 
 The helper, relevant symbols and executable checks . 
 The evidence chain can reach source without competing with the brief for attention. Only this review is declared as the primary artifact.

sections.heading: 03 Return a Comment
sections.text:
After reading, you can question a specific heading, figure or passage. The returned map identifies that target and the document version. HTML keeps the existing notes format; Markdown has a saved adjacent map for readers without inline comments. 
 03 · The return path 

 Read and remark 
Choose a passage and leave your words. → 
 Return the map 
Supply it with the document, or copy it while naming the brief. → 
 Resolve and answer 
The agent checks identity, version and target before responding. 
 A changed version or removed passage keeps its comment visibly unresolved. A heading rename preserves its explicit target; uncertainty about the version is retained. 

 The Markdown map example is editable text. Inline Markdown controls depend on the reader. In a standalone browser, HTML edits persist in browser storage; saving into the original file requires the host's supported write path.

sections.heading: 04 What Was Checked
sections.text:
The checks exercise the reader's loop as well as the stored data. They found and caught a browser serialization detail that initially made an unchanged saved page look like a new revision. 
 04 · Verification 

18 Python tests passed 
Preservation, malformed data, stale and missing targets, unknown revisions, explicit agreement and evidence links. 

968 / 390 Browser widths checked 
Real comment, reload, export, snapshot and rename rebuild. No page overflow or clipped SVG text. 
 The tests establish these cases in a separate headless browser. Native inline Markdown commenting and Terminal Delight's in-place writer were not exercised in this run. 
Measured by the Python and browser checks. Validation record . 

 Existing skills 
Their tracked files are unchanged. The new skill reads canonical assets and applies a guarded anchor adaptation in its own output. 
 Video later 
The README reserves pause, time-range comments, resume and agent handoff. No video annotation is implemented.
